content: As shown in Table TABREF26 , NCEL achieves the best performance in most cases with an average gain of 2% on Micro F1 and 3% Macro F1. The baseline methods also achieve competitive results on some datasets but fail to adapt to the others. For example, AIDA and xLisa perform quite well on ACE2004 but poorly on other datasets, or WAT, PBoH, and WNED have a favorable performance on CoNLL but lower values on ACE2004 and AQUAINT. Our proposed method performs consistently well on all datasets that demonstrates the good generalization ability.
